chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Kasula, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Shadzkuni, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, who said:

I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) say: 'On the Day of Doubt, we were commanded to fast it and forbidden from fasting it; we were commanded that a person should fast it on the assumption that it is from Sha'ban, and forbidden from fasting it on the assumption that it is from the month of Ramadan, while the crescent had not yet been seen.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the 30th of Sha'ban (Day of Doubt) before Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Sajjad (AS), transmitted through the chain of al-Zuhri, clarifies the juristic principle of 'taking precaution' (ihtiyat) regarding the Day of Doubt (Yawm al-Shakk). It establishes that fasting is permissible but must be performed as a voluntary act from Sha'ban rather than an obligatory one from Ramadan, reflecting the Shia emphasis on avoiding doubt in religious obligations until the moon is sighted. This ruling underscores the distinction between the certainty of the lunar calendar and the practical uncertainty faced by the community before official announcement.
